title: Implementation of an open psychodynamic group therapy in acute inpatient care: A study on acceptance, feasibility, and therapeutic relationship
summary:
This study investigates how well an open psychodynamic group therapy is accepted and can be implemented in routine clinical practice on an acute psychiatric inpatient ward. Adult patients who wish to participate voluntarily in the survey are eligible to take part. The aim is to determine whether the group intervention is experienced as helpful, whether participation is feasible, and how the therapeutic relationship within the group is perceived.
To this end, brief questionnaires are completed before and after a two-week period of participation in the group therapy. The treatment itself is not altered by the study. The results are intended to contribute to a better scientific evaluation and further development of low-threshold psychotherapeutic services for individuals experiencing acute mental health crises. Psychotherapeutic services are often too difficult to access for this vulnerable patient group, meaning that many affected individuals either do not gain sufficient access or discontinue existing treatments over time.
conditions: Mental disorders in an acute psychiatric setting; a transdiagnostic patient population undergoing acute inpatient psychiatric treatment is being studied.

interventions.name: Single-arm observational group without a control group, consisting of patients from an acute psychiatric inpatient unit who participate in a psychodynamic group therapy as part of their inpatient treatment. Prospective pre–post assessment among participants of the open psychodynamic group therapy us

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient treatment on ward Psy4, capacity to provide informed consent, sufficient proficiency in German, adequate visual and reading ability, and the ability to complete the questionnaires independently.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals under 18 years of age and adults who lack the capacity to provide informed consent for study participation.
